title: Noticeable delay in updating mouse position every time I click on MacOS
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.4.1-stable, 3.6.1-stable, 3.5.3-stable, and 3.3-stable
- I was unable to find a build that does not reproduce this, but some of the builds I wanted to try were missing from the download archive, i.e. the MacOS "Standard" build for 3.2.3-stable.

### System information

I have reproduced this in MacOS Sequoia 15.5 (24F74) on both an M3 Max Macbook Pro and an M1 Macbook Air. It is probably specific to Mac.

### Issue description

Initially I noticed that there seemed to be a bit of lag every time I try to drag something in my game on Mac. Digging deeper, I discovered that everything not related to mouse position was still running smoothly. I was getting the mouse position from InputEventMouse events, but even if I use get_global_mouse_position() in _process, there is a brief moment that the mouse position stops updating every time I click. I can reproduce this with a very minimal project (will detail in the next section), and even in the editor itself for all the 3.x versions I tested. 

In the editor, just clicking and dragging a node causes a brief hitch, which can cause the node I'm dragging to become significantly offset from my mouse pointer if I move quickly. I can't reproduce that offset in 4.4.1, but I think there is still a slight delay.

I did many experiments and the issue reproduced in every case:

- It happens in the editor, and in a non-debug export.
- It happens with Input.set_use_accumulated_input(true) or with Input.set_use_accumulated_input(false).
- It happens whether I'm getting the mouse position from get_global_mouse_position() in _process, or InputEventMouse type events as seen by either _input or a gui_input signal.

### Steps to reproduce

These steps are described for 3.5.3-stable. I haven't checked if anything differs for 4.x; I just upconverted my 3.x project. 

2. Create a new project
3. Select "User Interface" for the root node
4. Drag icon.png into the scene to add a Sprite child node called "Icon"
5. Attach a script to the root Control node
6. Add the following code:
```
onready var icon = $Icon
func _process(_delta):
	icon.position = get_global_mouse_position()
```

7. Save the scene
8. Run the project and select the current scene as the startup scene
9. Move your mouse around in the window - the sprite should follow
10. Click while moving - I observe the sprite stops following for a noticeable fraction of a second with each click.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[ClickMovementDelay.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21563956/ClickMovementDelay.zip)
